items.title: Local null normal pairs and the positive screen quotient
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure differential geometry of a spacelike surface and null hypersurface; no physical field equation or observation is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle convention in the
Lorentzian suppliers below. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be
a smooth embedded two-manifold without boundary whose induced form
$q:=\iota^*g$ is positive definite. Write
$$\mathcal N_pS:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,X)=0\text{ for every }X\in T_pS\}.$$
Then $\mathcal N S$ is a smooth rank-two Lorentzian vector bundle. Around each
$p\in S$ there are smooth future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with
$$g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0,\qquad g(\ell,k)=-2.$$
On an overlap where two such ordered pairs select the same future null ray,
they differ by a smooth boost $\ell'=e^f\ell$, $k'=e^{-f}k$; if their ray
labels are exchanged, the same rule holds after interchanging the labels.
No global null normal pair is asserted.

For a smooth null hypersurface $H$ with a smooth future null normal field
$\ell$ tangent to $H$, the quotient
$$\mathscr S_p:=\ell_p^\perp/\mathbb R\ell_p,\qquad p\in H,$$
is a smooth rank-two bundle with positive metric
$$\bar q_p([X],[Y]):=g_p(X,Y).$$
If $\ell$ is affinely geodesic, the map
$$B_p:\mathscr S_p\to\mathscr S_p,\qquad [X]\mapsto[\nabla_X\ell]$$
is well-defined and self-adjoint. On a spacelike section $S$ of $H$, the
quotient is isometric to $T_pS$. For a smooth future null normal $\ell$ to
$S$, define
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)\qquad(X,Y\in T_pS);$$
this is a well-defined symmetric bilinear form. Along an affine generator the
screen derivative $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$ is well-defined and
compatible with $\bar q$. Under a boost,
$$\chi_{e^f\ell}=e^f\chi_\ell.$$

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.2, 2.6-2.7, 4.4, and 5.1-5.6
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§5.4-5.5

items.title: Null normal pairs and screen geometry
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Geometric definitions only; no Einstein equation, stress-energy assumption, observation, or model-validity claim is included.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, for an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$, every curve $\lambda\mapsto F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed, null and affinely parametrized, and each map $F_\lambda:=F(\cdot,\lambda)$ is a spacelike immersion before its first focal instant. The field $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ is normal to each section and tangent to the immersed null hypersurface swept out by the curves. The parameter $\lambda$ is an affine parameter. On each section, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified with the tangent plane of that section. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

Before the first **focal instant**, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$ and is invertible. The first focal instant is the first positive $\lambda$ at which $A_\lambda$ loses rank. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. The derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$. The **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$, the **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and the **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint; equivalently its twist vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.2, 2.6-2.7, 4.4, 5.1, 5.5-5.8
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§5.4-5.5 and 8.5

items.title: Null Raychaudhuri and conjugate-point bound
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Conditional mathematical deduction from the stated Ricci inequality; no energy condition or Einstein equation is inferred.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Lorentzian supplier conventions. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let $S$ be a smooth spacelike two-surface, and let $F:U\times J\to M$ be a smooth null geodesic hypersurface congruence from an open section $U\subseteq S$, as defined in [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. Write $\ell=\partial_\lambda F$ and fix $p\in U$. Before the first focal instant let $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ be the screen Jacobi map, $B=A'A^{-1}$ the optical endomorphism, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}B$ its expansion, and $\sigma=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}$ its shear. Let $\operatorname{Ric}$ be the Ricci tensor in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then, along the generator $\gamma(\lambda)=F(p,\lambda)$ and before the first focal instant,
$$\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda}=-\frac{\theta^2}{2}-|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell).$$
If $\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)\ge0$ along the generator and $\theta(0)<0$, then a first focal instant occurs by affine parameter
$$\lambda_*=\frac{2}{|\theta(0)|},$$
provided the smooth congruence and generator are defined through $\lambda_*$. Here a focal instant means that the screen Jacobi map loses rank; the conclusion is local along this generator and asserts no curvature singularity.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§5.5-5.8 and 6.2
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§5.4-5.5 and 8.5

items.title: Null screen index form with a spacelike initial boundary
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure Lorentzian differential geometry; the result is a conditional second-variation identity and not an empirical statement.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian supplier conventions. Let
$S$ be a smooth spacelike embedded two-surface in a time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold. Let $\ell$ be a smooth future null normal field on a
neighborhood of $p$ in $S$, and let $\gamma:[0,L]\to M$ be a future affine
null geodesic normal to $S$ at $p=\gamma(0)$ with initial tangent $\ell(p)$.
Identify the positive
screen $\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ along the interval with an orthogonal
screen subbundle using a parallel null frame. For a screen field $V$, write
$D_\ell V$ for its screen covariant derivative and
$\mathcal R V:=[R(V,\ell)\ell]$. If $V,W$ are smooth screen fields with
$V(0),W(0)\in T_pS$ and $V(L)=W(L)=0$, define
$$I(V,W):=\int_0^L\bigl(\bar q(D_\ell V,D_\ell W)- \bar q(\mathcal RV,W)\bigr)\,d\lambda+ \chi_\ell(V(0),W(0)).$$
Then $I$ is a well-defined symmetric bilinear form. Every such $V$ is the
screen variational field of a smooth family of curves $F_s$ with
$F_s(0)\in S$, $F_s(L)=\gamma(L)$ and $F_0=\gamma$. For this family, with
$$E(s):=\frac12\int_0^L g(\partial_\lambda F_s,\partial_\lambda F_s)\,d\lambda,$$
the energy second variation is
$$E''(0)=I(V,V).$$

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.6-2.7 and 5.5-5.8
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§8.2 and 8.4

items.title: Null focal points exclude later horismos generators
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Local causal-geometric deduction; no completeness, curvature singularity, or empirical statement is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, as required by the supplied
causal-curve and push-up results. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $S$ be a smooth spacelike embedded
two-surface. Put $I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p)$,
$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p)$, and
$E^+(S):=J^+(S)\setminus I^+(S)$, using the causal-reachability conventions
of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let
$\gamma:[0,L_1]\to M$ be a future affinely parametrized null geodesic
orthogonal to $S$ at $p=\gamma(0)$, with initial tangent $\ell$ and null
second fundamental form $\chi_\ell$ as in
[[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]. A **focal instant** $\lambda_0>0$ is an
instant at which a nonzero screen Jacobi field arising from variation of the
initial point in $S$, with initial screen derivative determined by
$q^{-1}\chi_\ell$, has zero screen value.

If $\lambda_0$ is a focal instant, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$\gamma(\lambda)\in I^+(S)\qquad (\lambda_0<\lambda<\lambda_0+\varepsilon).$$
Consequently, no point on this portion of the generator belongs to
$E^+(S)$. The conclusion is local along the generator and does not assert
geodesic incompleteness or curvature blow-up. In an SI interpretation take
$x^0=ct$ and $\lambda$ in metres; the proof itself is independent of units.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.6-2.7 and 5.5-5.8
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§8.2 and 8.4-8.5

items.title: Round spheres in Minkowski spacetime
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical Minkowski example; no observation or field equation is used.
items.statement:
In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with length coordinates
$(t,\mathbf x)$ and metric $g=-dt^2+d\mathbf x^2$, let
$$S=\{(0,R\omega):\omega\in\mathbb S^2\},\qquad R>0.$$
The future null normals
$\ell=\partial_t+\partial_r$ and $k=\partial_t-\partial_r$ satisfy
$g(\ell,k)=-2$ and have expansions
$$\theta_\ell=\frac2R,\qquad \theta_k=-\frac2R.$$
Along the inward congruence generated by $k$, the screen Jacobi map is
$A_\lambda=(1-\lambda/R)\operatorname{id}$, so its first focal instant is
$\lambda=R$. The affine focusing bound from
[[prop-gr-fx-null-raychaudhuri]] is attained, and every point
$\gamma_\omega(\lambda)=(\lambda,(R-\lambda)\omega)$ with
$R<\lambda<3R$ lies in $I^+(S)$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.2, 5.5-5.8
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§5.4-5.5 and 8.5

items.title: Boost normalization and affine focusing
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical normalization example; no field equation or empirical claim is used.
items.statement:
Let $(\ell,k)$ be a normalized future null normal pair and let $f$ be a real
function on the initial section. Extend $f$ constantly along each affine
generator and boost the pair by $\ell'=e^f\ell$, $k'=e^{-f}k$. Then
$\widehat\theta_0=e^f\theta_0$, so the sign of the initial expansion is independent
of this positive normalization. Along each generator the new affine
parameter is $\lambda'=e^{-f}\lambda$; optical expansion, shear and Ricci
contraction scale so that the null Raychaudhuri equation is unchanged. A
focal event and its exclusion from $E^+(S)$ after the event are therefore
independent of the chosen constant-along-generator boost, although the
numerical affine focusing bound rescales to
$\lambda'_* = e^{-f}2/|\theta_0|$.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon and J. L. Jaramillo, A 3+1 perspective on null hypersurfaces and isolated horizons, Physics Reports 423 (2006), arXiv:gr-qc/0503113v2: §§2.6-2.7 and 5.1, 5.5-5.8
Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, full 106-page PDF: §§5.4-5.5 and 8.5
